general_reader_answers.contribution: The defensible contribution is a narrow operational integration: pairing-specific black-box evidence gates plus result-independent statistical claim consequences. Rollout Cards, trace assurance, AEVAL, common-random-number theory, and event-keyed randomness already supply the principal preservation, testing, trace, and coupling components separately.
general_reader_answers.effectiveness_result: The synthetic suite detects its designed failure modes; the restricted case has zero mismatches across 1,000 preflight units and 3,000 executions, but 99 of 200 timed-search clusters disagree, and the historical favorable-looking comparison is withheld under a retrospective rule. The later fixed-battery factorial contrast is unresolved and is reported descriptively.
general_reader_answers.limitation: The real engine has no semantic event identifiers, raw restricted traces are unavailable, the factorial rows were not trace repeated, the generic admission taxonomy was added after acquisition, and the public verifier cannot yet admit successful Level 6 or Level 7 evidence.
general_reader_answers.problem: A shared recorded seed can identify a matched schedule without showing that either agent repeats across execution contexts or that divergent policies receive the same random quantities for the same semantic events, so paired statistical wording can be unsupported.
general_reader_answers.protocol: The protocol hashes artifacts and boundary seeds, verifies row schedules, repeats identical arms at a declared trace-projection level across process and worker contexts, inventories stochastic sources, seeks semantic event alignment, and maps the resulting gate prefix to permitted or suppressed claims.

independence_attestation: I developed this assessment independently, without access to another reviewer assessment or any other reviewer output.
major_issues: M1 — Upper-gate operationalization is incomplete. The public file-bound `admit` interface cannot represent a successful Level 6 or Level 7 case: `release/protocol/evidence_bundle_schema.json` fixes the stochastic-source audit to `unavailable` and cross-arm event alignment to `not_applicable`, while `release/pevl_bench/evidence.py` derives those same states unconditionally. Only the unverified trusted-state classifier or the synthetic adapter can reach `seed_matched_bounded` or `event_aligned`. The package therefore does not yet machine-verify the two upper gates that distinguish its central statistical-admission contribution.

M2 — The advertised generic admission taxonomy has not been prospectively validated. It was created after acquisition, the descriptive-only reinterpretation was also post-acquisition, and the favorable-looking historical comparison was suppressed under a rule frozen only after those outcomes existed. The prospective case validates narrower binary acquisition/suppression gates, not prospective effectiveness of the generic multi-level claim map. This is honest in the manuscript, but it materially limits a Protocol Article claim that the integrated method has proved effective.

M3 — The real case does not validate pairing assumptions on the rows used for its policy contrast. Trace qualification used different preflight seed ranges, factorial candidate rows contain no trace digests, and the engine exposes no semantic event identifiers. The factorial therefore rests on a transfer assumption plus repeated-control available-record parity; it demonstrates a fixed-schedule description, not verified stochastic pairing of the comparison trajectories. For agent evaluation, the empirical evidence is strongest as a repeatability diagnostic and claim-limitation example.

M4 — The contribution remains distinct, but only narrowly, and the manuscript's close-work comparison is too compressed for that narrow boundary. Rollout Cards preserves rollout evidence and reporting/drop rules; trace assurance supplies contracts, replay, fault injection, localization, and governance; AEVAL supplies deterministic evaluation contracts and first-attempt evidence. This package adds pairing-specific gates and statistical claim consequences, but its restricted case retains only trace digests and omits promised localization and timing outputs. The manuscript should compare evidence units, trust boundaries, and decision consequences directly rather than mainly stating what each neighbor lacks.

M5 — The article-level reproduction attestation is stale and currently unverifiable. `REPRODUCTION_REPORT.json` is schema version 1, names the earlier trace-based title, records a 10-page PDF and obsolete artifact hashes, while the current manuscript has 13 pages; `scripts/verify_reproduction_report.py` requires a schema-v2 report and fails because `REPRODUCTION_REPORT.sha256` is absent. The release-level processed-data verifier passes, but the canonical article-level reproduction record is not bound to this reviewed package.
minor_issues: m1 — Stage 6 inventories many static clock, randomness, global-state, and native-state hits while two engine binaries remain unassessed, but the protocol does not provide an objective rule for resolving a hit, declaring an unresolved invalidator, or deciding that this gate passes. The adoption guidance should specify those outcomes and their evidence.

m2 — The public evidence schema hard-codes one schedule vocabulary and three execution-profile names, including `workers-8-reverse`. A reusable agent-evaluation protocol needs a documented, validated way to declare other worker counts, enqueue orders, process lifecycles, trace projections, and schedule fields without editing core code unsafely.

m3 — The phrase `complete recorded trace projection` is carefully qualified in the definitions, but readers cannot inspect the raw projection and the promised first-divergence/actor and timing summaries are absent. Every empirical use of `complete` should continue to name the included fields and make clear that digest equality is not trace-content verification by an external reader.

m4 — The release correctly states that its dependency files are direct-package declarations rather than transitive locks and that no fresh clean-environment build is evidenced. This should be closed before an acceptance-stage reproducibility claim, even though the present release verifier runs successfully in the available environment.
required_fixes: R1 — Extend the file-bound evidence schema and verifier with closed, testable record types for completed stochastic-source audits and cross-arm event-alignment evidence, including certificates and an external provenance anchor; otherwise narrow every `executable admission` claim to the gates the public path actually verifies.

R2 — Prospectively freeze and exercise the generic claim taxonomy, inputs, estimands, and consequences in an end-to-end held-out application. If no new acquisition is feasible, present it explicitly as a post-acquisition formalization/proposed template and avoid implying that its multi-level operation has itself been prospectively validated.

R3 — Either collect the declared trace projection on the actual comparison rows under the same acquisition schedule or narrow the empirical conclusion to transfer-qualified repeatability diagnostics and schedule-indexed description. Do not let preflight on different seeds stand in for observed pairing evidence on factorial rows.

R4 — Expand the close-work section into an explicit comparison of evidence unit, trace retention, trust anchor, pairing scope, decision consequence, and empirical validation for Rollout Cards, trace assurance, AEVAL, and this protocol. State clearly which mechanisms are borrowed and that the remaining contribution is the pairing-specific evidence-to-claim integration.

R5 — Regenerate a schema-v2 `REPRODUCTION_REPORT.json` and its SHA-256 sidecar against the current 13-page manuscript, PDF, novelty audit, release manifest, and completed reviews; make `verify_reproduction_report.py` pass in a clean committed state.

R6 — Specify operational Stage-6 pass/fail/unavailable criteria and remediation for each source-audit category, and document a safe schema-level method for adapting execution profiles and schedule fields to other agent-evaluation systems.

R7 — Resolve or formally sign the promised-output deviation, and either release independently verifiable localization/timing evidence under lawful access or keep those endpoints explicitly unavailable in all protocol-completeness claims.
